description: Animates a SCALAR clip parameter (e.g. Opacity, Scale, Rotation) from a start value to an end value along an eased curve, by baking a dense run of keyframes whose values trace the easing shape. This is the honest path to eased motion: Premiere lets script SET a keyframe interpolation type but exposes no getter to read it back, and never exposed the temporal-ease amount to script at all — so a native "set the ease" call cannot be verified. Baked keyframe VALUES are readable back, so every written point is verified. Supports Penner easings and a CSS-style cubic-bezier. Scalar parameters only (multi-dimensional params like Position are refused).

bezier.description: CSS-style cubic-bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2]; overrides easing. x1 and x2 must be within [0, 1]

componentName.description: The display name of the component (e.g., "Motion", "Opacity")

easing.description: Named easing curve; ignored when bezier is provided

endTime.description: Clip-local end time in seconds (must be greater than startTime)

paramName.description: The display name of the scalar parameter to animate (e.g., "Opacity", "Scale", "Rotation")

samples.description: Number of segments between the endpoints; keyframes written = samples + 1

name: bake_keyframe_ease
